course.title: Atomic – Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics — Stage 8

unit.title: Probability
unit.blurb: Equally likely outcomes, mutually exclusive events, the probability of an event not happening, and comparing experimental with theoretical probability.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Calculate probabilities of equally likely outcomes and use the fact that probabilities of mutually exclusive outcomes add to 1.

O2.t: Find experimental probabilities (relative frequencies) and compare them with theoretical probabilities.

p: **P(event) = number of favourable outcomes ÷ total number of outcomes**, when all outcomes are equally likely.
Probabilities go from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). **P(not A) = 1 − P(A)**.

lesson.q: A bag has 3 red, 5 blue and 2 green counters. One is taken at random. Find P(blue) and P(not blue).

p: Outcomes that cannot happen at the same time are **mutually exclusive**. The probabilities of all the mutually exclusive outcomes add up to **1**.
If P(red) = 0.3 and P(blue) = 0.5 and these are the only colours with green, then P(green) = 1 − 0.3 − 0.5 = 0.2.

p: **Experimental probability** (relative frequency) = number of times the event happened ÷ number of trials.
The **theoretical probability** is worked out from equally likely outcomes. With more trials the experimental probability usually gets **closer** to the theoretical one.

lesson.q: A coin is tossed 80 times and lands heads 46 times. Find the experimental probability of heads.

p: **Expected number = probability × number of trials**. A fair dice rolled 120 times: expect 120 × 1/6 = 20 sixes.
Experimental results do not have to match the expected number exactly; they vary by chance.
